proposed.text: A developer owns a 1,800 sq m building straddling the boundary between a Fire Restrictive Zone and a Highly Fire Restrictive Zone. Of the total floor area, 650 sq m are within the Highly Fire Restrictive Zone and 1,150 sq m are in the Fire Restrictive Zone. Which statement correctly describes the applicable fire zone requirements under PD 1096 Rule V, Sec. 502?

options.text: The building must comply with Fire Restrictive Zone requirements for the 1,150 sq m portion and Highly Fire Restrictive Zone requirements for the 650 sq m portion, treated independently
The building must comply with Fire Restrictive Zone requirements because the majority of its floor area (1,150 sq m) is located in that zone, following the predominant-area rule
The building must comply with Highly Fire Restrictive Zone requirements for the entire building, because more than one-third of its total floor area is in that zone
The Building Official has discretion to determine which zone applies based on the building's occupancy classification and the fire safety features provided in the design

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: This is the 'NRH' split-zone rule. The threshold is 'more than one-third' — not a simple majority. 650/1800 = 36.1%, which exceeds 33.3%. The entire building follows the restrictive zone.
